items.statement: Submitting a RESET bdev I/O clears its cached I/O path, starts bdev_nvme_reset, and returns without generic completion handling.
Each controller reset is dispatched to the app thread, where the handler selects a reset function, records the completion callback, and invokes that function.
A busy controller queues the reset I/O and returns; an already-disabled controller is treated as success, while other negative reset-selection results are propagated.
Reset freezes every bdev channel by setting resetting, and any successful controller reset changes the aggregate bdev reset result from failed to successful.
Completion removes every retained I/O from pending_resets, then aborts retry I/Os and clears resetting while unfreezing each bdev channel.
Among negative reset-selection results, only EALREADY is normalized to success; every other negative value remains an error passed to reset continuation.
When a second reset is submitted from another thread while the first controller reset is active, the second bdev I/O becomes the first entry in pending_resets.
A failed controller reset resumes all queued resets with failure, and controller removal during an active reset makes both the active and concurrent reset I/Os fail.
Controller reset completion repeatedly removes the head of pending_resets and resumes that bdev I/O with the controller-reset outcome.
items.description: Reset completion repeatedly removes the first pending reset from the controller queue and resumes it with the controller-reset result.
